sections.html:
Fremont is the county seat of Dodge County in eastern Nebraska. It had 27,141 residents in the 2020 census and an estimated 28,350 in 2025, which makes it the sixth most populous city in the state. The city covers about 10.8 square miles of land. North Bend had 1,263 residents, Scribner 814 and Hooper 793, and 5,085 people, 13 percent of the county, live outside any town.

Dodge County has 16,725 housing units and 15,168 households, with 65.0 percent of homes owner-occupied. The median home price was $217,210 in the fourth quarter of 2025. Dodge County issued 41 permits for detached single-family homes in 2024 and 6 for other housing units. That is a small number for a county of 38,057 people, so most buyers are choosing among existing houses.

Meatpacking, health care, schools and agriculture have long been the biggest employers. Hormel Foods has been first on local lists with an estimated 1,000 to 1,500 workers, followed by Fremont Health Medical Center, Fremont Public Schools and Nye Health Services. A Costco-backed poultry complex, Lincoln Premium Poultry, started construction in 2019.

Grain is a visible business too. ADM has two Fremont elevators, and Norag, Scoular and Viterra also have elevators in the county. A shift change at a large plant can send a house to market in a hurry.

Fremont Public Schools is one of five school districts in Dodge County. The others are Howells-Dodge Consolidated, Logan View, Scribner-Snyder and West Point Public Schools. Midland University is the city's four-year college, and Dodge County is in the Metropolitan Community College service area.

sections.h2: Which Dodge County offices handle property tax
sections.html:
The Assessor, Treasurer and Register of Deeds work at the Dodge County Courthouse, 435 N Park Avenue in Fremont. Courthouse hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, and the county board meets every other Wednesday.

  • Assessor: Room 202, 402-727-3911, open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Treasurer: mail to PO Box 999, Fremont, NE 68026. The line for real estate and personal property taxes is 402-727-2750.
  • Register of Deeds: records the deed after a sale.

The county levy was $0.221 per $100, which raised $14,727,024 of the $89,875,353 levied by all local governments on taxable valuation of $6,311,522,302. That puts the county's own share near 16 percent. Schools, the city and other districts add to it.

Fremont has its own municipal electric service, listed as City of Fremont alongside Omaha PPD, Burt County PPD and Cuming County PPD for other parts of Dodge County. Dodge County is a zoned county, and the Lower Elkhorn and Lower Platte North natural resource districts both reach into it. The county counts 726 rural drinking water wells, 1,745 irrigation and livestock wells, and 111 surface water diversions for irrigation.

The county links live stream gauges for the Platte River at North Bend and near Fremont, along with Logan Creek and Maple Creek. It owns 264 bridges and one dam, so the condition of the county road that serves an acreage is a fair question to raise early. A seller on acreage near a stream should expect questions from buyers and lenders about flood history and be ready with answers.

Look up the current tax bill with the Dodge County Treasurer before you set a date, and ask the closing agent how taxes and any utility balances will be settled. The title company takes the payoff from your proceeds, so an unpaid balance does not have to stop a sale, but it should be known early.

sections.h2: What a Fremont seller owes at closing
sections.html:
The seller owes the state's documentary stamp tax under section 76-901, set at $3.32 per $1,000 of value for deeds before January 1, 2032. It drops to $2.32 per $1,000 on transfers from that date forward.

Under section 76-2,120, the seller must hand over a signed condition statement by the time a contract binds the buyer, and must correct it if something changes beforehand. Court-ordered transfers, foreclosure sales and transfers to a spouse or lineal relative are among the listed exceptions.

  • Order a payoff letter from each lender.
  • Look up the current tax bill with the Dodge County Treasurer.
  • Ask the closing agent how taxes and any utility balances will be settled.

sections.h2: Step by step if you want to sell
sections.html:
The path from decision to closing is short when you do the groundwork first.

  • Call the Dodge County Treasurer at 402-727-2750 and ask for the current balance on the parcel.
  • Ask the Assessor at 402-727-3911 how the property is classified and valued.
  • If the house is on an acreage, gather what you know about wells, nearby streams and the county road that serves it.
  • Request a payoff letter from each lender with a claim on the house.
  • Complete the written condition statement and update it if anything changes before the contract is signed.

Each of these also answers a question a buyer or lender is likely to ask.

Some Fremont sales begin with a house that has been in a family for years, or a rental that needs more than the owner wants to spend. Both situations are easier when the paperwork is in one place.

Bring papers that show who is allowed to sign for the property, a recent tax statement and any past repair records. Transfers to a spouse or lineal relative are among the exceptions to the condition statement, but the stamp tax rules are separate, so ask the closing agent which apply to you.

A cash sale skips the buyer's loan, which means no bank appraisal and no underwriting delay. You still pay the stamp tax, settle the tax balance and sign the deed. What you gain is a closing date that rests on title work, not on a lender's schedule, which helps when a job change or a bad repair bill is driving the sale.

Fremont buyers are mostly people choosing among existing houses, since new construction is limited. Many work in meatpacking, health care, schools or agriculture. A seller who can show a clear tax balance, a signed condition statement and a recorded deed in the right name tends to close with fewer delays.

If the house is near the Platte River or one of the creeks, be ready to talk about flood history. If it is an acreage, be ready to talk about the well and the county road that serves it.

faqs.q: Who do I call about property tax in Fremont?
faqs.a: The Dodge County Treasurer handles billing. Call 402-727-2750 for real estate and personal property taxes, or write to PO Box 999, Fremont, NE 68026. Valuation questions go to the Assessor at 402-727-3911.

faqs.q: Is Dodge County a zoned county?
faqs.a: Yes. Dodge County is zoned, and inside Fremont city rules apply as well.

faqs.q: What is the largest employer in Fremont?
faqs.a: Hormel Foods has been first on local lists, with an estimated 1,000 to 1,500 employees. Fremont Health Medical Center, Fremont Public Schools and Nye Health Services follow.

faqs.q: How much stamp tax will I pay when I sell my Fremont house?
faqs.a: For deeds before January 1, 2032, the seller pays $3.32 for each $1,000 of value. The rate drops to $2.32 after that.
Midland University is in Fremont. Dodge County is in the Metropolitan Community College service area.
